plugin.kube.description: Clusters on the servers your keys reach, found without a kubeconfig in sight
err.emptyPattern: An empty pattern in the item {item}
err.patternBadPort: The pattern {pattern}: the port {port} is not a number
err.patternEmptyPart: The pattern {pattern} in the item {item}: an empty login or host
err.sshBadHost: That is not a host name
err.sshBadPortField: The key “{key}” has a port that is not a number: {port}
err.sshConfigUnreadable: ~/.ssh/config at {path} will not read, so it is not trusted for anything
err.sshHostKeyChanged: The host key of {host}:{port} has changed. It now presents {fingerprint}. This is what an attack in the middle looks like, so nothing was signed. If the server was really reinstalled, forget the old key and connect again.
err.sshHostKeyDeclined: The key of {host} was not trusted ({fingerprint}); the connection was dropped
err.sshHostKeyNotPinned: The key {host} presented is not the one pinned in the item (kw-hostkey). It presented {fingerprint}. Nothing was signed.
err.sshKeyGone: The key is no longer in the vault
err.sshKnownHostsUnreadable: The host keys file {path} will not read, so no host can be checked against it
err.sshKnownHostsUnwritable: The host key could not be saved to {path}
err.sshLoginRequired: Which login on {host}? Type it, or write it into the route as login@{host}
err.sshNoPublicKey: The key “{key}” has no public half to offer
err.sshNotSsh: {host} answered, but not as an ssh server
err.sshProxyJumpUnsupported: {host} is reached through {jump} (ProxyJump in ~/.ssh/config); the terminal does not go through jump hosts yet
err.sshTimedOutLogin: {host} did not answer the sign-in within {seconds} s
err.sshLinkGone: The terminal lost its sealed link; open the session again
err.linkGone: The sealed link to the plugin is gone; open the screen again
err.sshJumpUnsupported: {host} is reached through {jump} (ProxyJump in ~/.ssh/config), and going through jump hosts is not supported yet
err.sshOutputTooLong: {host} answered with more than {max} bytes, which is not what was asked for
err.sshTimedOutCommand: {host} did not finish the command within {seconds} s
err.kubeAuthUnsupported: This context signs in through a program (exec or an auth provider), which is not supported yet: running a program a kubeconfig names is not something to do behind your back
err.kubeBadPath: The kubeconfig names a file with a path that cannot be read safely
err.kubeBroken: The Kubernetes plugin broke inside; open the section again
err.kubeConfigIncomplete: The kubeconfig is incomplete: {missing} is named but not described
err.kubeDetectGarbled: The server answered the cluster check with something it could not have said: {line}
err.kubeForbidden: Your account in the cluster may not list {kind}
err.kubeForeignFile: The kubeconfig names a file that was not read from its server
err.kubeInsecure: The kubeconfig turns TLS checks off for {server}; such a cluster is not opened
err.kubeNeedsSudo: The kubeconfig is readable only by root, and sudo asks for a password. Allow this login to read it, or let it run sudo without a password for this file
err.kubeNoCluster: That cluster is not known; look at its server again
err.kubeNoContext: The kubeconfig does not say which context to use
err.kubeNoServer: That server is not among the ones your keys reach
err.kubeNotFound: There is no such {kind} any more
err.kubeNotOpen: The cluster is not open; open it again
err.kubePlainHttp: The kubeconfig talks to {server} in plain HTTP, which would carry the credentials in the clear
err.kubeProxyUnsupported: The kubeconfig goes through a proxy (proxy-url), which is not supported yet
err.kubeReadFailed: The kubeconfig could not be read on {host}
err.kubeScanRunning: A look at the servers is already under way
err.kubeSecretNotShown: A secret's data is not shown
err.kubeTimedOut: The cluster did not answer within {seconds} s
err.kubeTunnelRefused: The server would not open a way to the API at {address}: {reason}
err.kubeUnauthorized: The cluster does not accept the kubeconfig's credentials
err.kubeUnreachable: The cluster's API cannot be reached: {reason}
kube.noClustersYet: No clusters yet. Look at the servers to find them.
kube.serversExplain: Every server a key reaches is looked at for k3s, RKE2, kubeadm, k0s, MicroK8s and ~/.kube/config. Each look signs in with your finger; nothing is looked at by itself.
kube.trustExplain: {host} is not known yet. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server's owner gives you; trusting it saves it in the key's item.
kube.proxiedHint: Reached through {jump}; going through jump hosts is not supported yet
kube.noServers.title: No servers to look at
kube.noServers.body: Bind an ssh key to a host in the SSH section or on the key's card, and the server shows up here.
kube.openingSsh: Signing in to the server and reading its kubeconfig. Confirm the sign-in with your finger.
kube.col.name: Name
kube.secretHidden: A secret's data is not fetched: it never leaves the cluster through keyward.
err.kubeBadScale: Replicas are set for a Deployment or a StatefulSet, from 0 to 1000
err.kubeKindNotSupported: keyward does not change objects of kind {kind}
err.kubeLocalFileUnreadable: A file ~/.kube/config names will not read: {path}
err.kubeManifestNoKind: The manifest does not say its apiVersion and kind
err.kubeManifestNoNamespace: The manifest needs a namespace: pick one or write metadata.namespace
err.sshPortRequired: {host} has no port set up: write it into the route (host:port), the item's kw-port or ~/.ssh/config
kube.unsetHint: Login and port are needed: without them keyward does not connect
kube.addYamlHint: Paste the YAML. It is kept encrypted as a note in the vault, never as a file
kube.deleteHint: It is removed from the cluster. Type its name to confirm
kube.tpl.roleBinding: RoleBinding: give a role to a user
kube.searchHint: Search: api ns:payments status:pending ready:no age:1h
err.kubeTooManyShells: Too many shells are open; close one first
kube.tpl.service: Service: in front of an app
